original_question: How does one systematically produce examples of a contact 3-manifold (M, ξ), a line field L tangent to ξ, and a nonvanishing closed 2-form ω, of integral class, annihilating L?
target_in_paper: Question 2.15 in §2.5 (Engel structures), posed immediately after the paragraph introducing Mitsumatsu’s prequantum prolongation. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already lands on the exact problem stated in the paper: it asks for precisely the same data, namely a contact 3-manifold (M, ξ), a line field L tangent to ξ, and a nowhere-vanishing closed 2-form ω of integral class annihilating L. It therefore captures the intended Engel-geometry problem rather than a broader neighboring question. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
missing_details: Make explicit that this is the input data for Mitsumatsu’s prequantum prolongation construction of Engel structures; that nearby motivation is part of the paper’s intent. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

Spell out that 'a line field L tangent to ξ' means a smooth rank-1 subbundle L ⊂ ξ ⊂ TM. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

Spell out that 'ω is of integral class' means its de Rham class [ω] lies in the image of H^2(M; Z) → H^2(M; R). ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
Spell out that 'ω annihilates L' means ι_Xω = 0 for every local nonzero section X of L. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

If you want the question to be fully stand-alone, it helps to mention the nearby output of the construction: the associated S^1-bundle over M with curvature ω, whose connection and lifted distributions produce the Engel manifold. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

There are no hidden coefficient-field, degree, homogeneity, nilpotency, or 'for sufficiently large m' issues here; the only implicit items are the geometric meanings of L, [ω], and annihilation. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
refined_question: Can one give a general construction scheme, serving as input to Mitsumatsu’s prequantum prolongation, for triples ((M, ξ), L, ω) where M is a smooth 3-manifold with contact plane field ξ, L ⊂ ξ is a smooth line field, and ω is a nowhere-vanishing closed 2-form on M whose de Rham class [ω] is integral and such that ι_Xω = 0 for every local nonzero section X of L? ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
justification: The nearest official formulation is exactly Question 2.15 in §2.5. The paragraph immediately before it supplies the hidden context and notation: these data are precisely the input for Mitsumatsu’s prequantum prolongation, which outputs an Engel structure on an S^1-bundle over M with curvature ω; it also notes that the hypotheses imply L is spanned by a volume-preserving vector field. The short remark after the question speculates that the integrality assumption might perhaps be removable by perturbing and scaling ω, but the paper does not present that as an equivalent reformulation. So the faithful refinement is to keep the scope exactly at Question 2.15 and only unpack the geometric meanings needed to make it self-contained. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
